nodes.label: Structural AST extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic code extraction avoids LLM costs and API-key requirements.

nodes.label: Semantic extraction
nodes.rationale: Documents, papers, and images need semantic interpretation beyond code structure.

nodes.label: Host agent semantic fallback
nodes.rationale: Uses the running agent when Gemini credentials are absent, avoiding a mandatory API key.

nodes.label: Prompt-versioned semantic cache
nodes.rationale: Cache reads and writes use the same extraction prompt so prompt upgrades invalidate old results without losing unchanged-prompt hits.

nodes.label: AST and semantic merge
nodes.rationale: AST nodes take precedence during ID deduplication while semantic relationships augment the structural graph.

nodes.label: Community detection
nodes.rationale: Surfaces cross-document connections and supplies navigable groups.

nodes.label: Graph health check
nodes.rationale: Read-only diagnostics expose collapsed edges, missing endpoints, and self-loops without aborting a usable graph.

nodes.label: Graph shrink guard
nodes.rationale: Refuses empty or smaller exports to protect an existing graph and keep its report consistent.

nodes.label: Output-gated semantic manifest
nodes.rationale: Only successful semantic extractions are stamped; failed or omitted chunks remain eligible for retry.

nodes.label: Directed graph mode
nodes.rationale: Preserves source-to-target orientation and reciprocal relationships.

nodes.label: Obsidian vault export
nodes.rationale: Explicit opt-in avoids creating one file per graph node by default.

nodes.label: Folder watcher
nodes.rationale: Code changes rebuild structurally; semantic changes flag a manual update rather than invoking an LLM automatically.

nodes.label: Three-second debounce
nodes.rationale: Waits for write activity to settle so parallel agent writes do not trigger one rebuild per file.

nodes.label: OpenCypher MERGE export
nodes.rationale: MERGE supports repeated imports without duplicate creation; FalkorDB needs statement-by-statement loading.

nodes.label: Token-reduction benchmark
nodes.rationale: Runs above 5000 corpus words; smaller corpora benefit primarily from structural clarity.

nodes.label: Extraction confidence rubric
nodes.rationale: Separates explicit, inferred, and ambiguous relationships with auditable numeric confidence.

nodes.label: Full-path deterministic node IDs
nodes.rationale: Full repository-relative paths avoid ghost duplicates and collisions between same-named files.

nodes.label: Absolute source provenance
nodes.rationale: Verbatim absolute source paths let downstream full and incremental builds normalize to the same base.

nodes.label: Hyperedges
nodes.rationale: Represent shared flows involving at least three nodes when pairwise relationships lose group information.

nodes.label: Concept rationale attributes
nodes.rationale: Attach design intent to named concepts rather than introducing artificial rationale nodes.

nodes.label: GitHub clone and cross-repo merge reference
Reusable GitHub clones
nodes.rationale: Stores clones under ~/.graphify/repos and reuses them on repeated runs.

nodes.label: Cross-repository graph merge
nodes.rationale: Combines graph files while retaining each node's repo origin.

nodes.label: Per-subfolder CLI extraction
nodes.rationale: Writes outputs within scanned subfolders to avoid clobbering the skill's shared cwd output directory.

nodes.label: Commit hook and CLAUDE integration reference
Post-commit graph rebuild
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds changed code after a commit without a background watcher, appending to existing hooks.

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md graph integration
nodes.rationale: Adds graph-first codebase guidance so future Claude Code sessions need no explicit Graphify invocation.

nodes.label: Constrained vocabulary expansion
nodes.rationale: The literal matcher lacks stemming, synonyms, and cross-language matching; selecting existing graph tokens makes expansion auditable.

nodes.label: Breadth-first traversal
nodes.rationale: Nearest-neighbor traversal gives broad context; the inline fallback explores three layers.

nodes.label: Depth-first traversal
nodes.rationale: Traces specific dependency chains; the inline fallback limits depth to six.

nodes.label: Save-result feedback loop
nodes.rationale: Saved answers, cited nodes, and expanded terms become context for subsequent updates.

nodes.label: Work memory reflections
nodes.rationale: Useful sources, dead ends, and corrected answers help future sessions avoid repeating failed investigations.

nodes.label: Graph-informed transcription prompt
nodes.rationale: God-node labels supply a domain hint without a separate API call; video-only corpora use a generic punctuation prompt.

nodes.label: Incremental re-extraction
nodes.rationale: Re-extracting only changed files saves time and tokens.

nodes.label: Replace-on-re-extract merge
nodes.rationale: Changed sources replace prior nodes while only genuinely deleted sources are pruned, preventing both stale nodes and deletion of fresh output.

nodes.label: Portable manifest paths
nodes.rationale: Manifest and graph paths share a scan-root-relative base so moved clones continue matching cached files.

nodes.label: Failed semantic chunk retry
nodes.rationale: Clearing stale semantic hashes for unstamped files ensures failed chunks are requeued.

nodes.label: Cluster-only rebuild
nodes.rationale: Re-clusters and regenerates final outputs without relying on temporary extraction files deleted by earlier cleanup.

nodes.label: First-session outcome
nodes.rationale: Captures progress from installation failure through returning for another useful task.

nodes.label: Public feedback redaction
nodes.rationale: Public issues must omit credentials, private code, and personal information.

nodes.label: Named participants
nodes.rationale: Separate vendor conversations can review one another through explicitly addressed messages.

nodes.label: Autonomous subagents
nodes.rationale: Focused background assignments allow independent work while the owning agent continues.

nodes.label: Subagent Git worktrees
nodes.rationale: Optional branches isolate edits from the project and other agents; uncommitted and ignored files are not carried over.

nodes.label: Subagent completion reports
nodes.rationale: Full reports expose changes, failures, and branch location and resume the owner ahead of queued follow-ups.

nodes.label: Automatic checkpoints
nodes.rationale: A separate local Git repository permits file and chat restoration without touching the project's history or staging.

nodes.label: Persistent memory
nodes.rationale: Locally stored preferences and project decisions survive sessions and can be retrieved by meaning.

nodes.label: Global memory
nodes.rationale: Carries preferences across projects.

nodes.label: Project memory
nodes.rationale: Scopes durable decisions to the session directory.

nodes.label: Runtime context compaction
nodes.rationale: Each vendor runtime folds its own history when its context window fills and records the reported summary.

nodes.label: Persistent sessions
nodes.rationale: Preserve directory, conversation, participants, models, and permission mode across task switches and restarts.

nodes.label: Repository instruction discovery
nodes.rationale: Session-directory SIRUS.md replaces AGENTS.md; guidance is fixed at runtime start and is subordinate to user requests and tool permissions.

nodes.label: Vendor-native skills
nodes.rationale: Routes skill invocations through Claude Code or Codex in each vendor's own format and discovery rules.

nodes.label: Session permission modes
nodes.rationale: Auto, ask, and bypass apply through vendor runtimes to both participants and subagents.

nodes.label: Multiple provider accounts
nodes.rationale: Supports existing subscriptions and API keys together, with fallback to configured sources for the same provider.

nodes.label: Optional installation statistics
nodes.rationale: Counts active installations using a minimal payload and non-blocking network requests; arbitrary public submissions make counts estimates.

nodes.label: Random installation identifier
nodes.rationale: A local random 128-bit identifier avoids hardware identifiers and account details.

nodes.label: HMAC-SHA-256 installation digest
nodes.rationale: Only the keyed digest is stored, never the client installation ID.

nodes.label: 35-day retention cleanup
nodes.rationale: Daily scheduled cleanup deletes old records to bound retained installation history.

nodes.label: Dashboard CORS origin
nodes.rationale: Allows the dashboard to read stats when Worker origin configuration matches GitHub Pages or permits public access.

nodes.label: Small read-heavy workload design
nodes.rationale: Intended for small Workers/D1 workloads; deployment guidance calls for checking quotas and failing closed or adopting a paid plan if they are exceeded.

nodes.label: Session facade
nodes.rationale: Described implementation: owns one conversation and delegates transcripts, routing, rounds, checkpoints, queue and notifications to independently constructible collaborators.

nodes.label: Per-participant Transcript
nodes.rationale: Only addressed entries and the participant's own responses enter its record; one delivered entry object can be shared by several transcripts.

nodes.label: Timeline
nodes.rationale: Allocates session-wide sequence numbers and merges participant transcripts into an ordered UI and snapshot view; owns assistant-entry identity.

nodes.label: ParticipantRoster
nodes.rationale: Owns participants and the single @name mention grammar.

nodes.label: TurnRunner
nodes.rationale: Runs addressed participants in parallel and delivers whole attributed messages to mentioned peers in subsequent rounds; owns participant-introduction text.

nodes.label: CheckpointLog and DirectoryActivity
nodes.rationale: The pre-turn checkpoint is awaited before prompting because native vendor tools cannot wait on Sirus's mutation barrier. Chat rewinds truncate all transcripts by sequence and rebuild runtimes; worktree workers do not block project-file rewind.

nodes.label: MessageQueue
nodes.rationale: One isAutoSendable predicate governs automatic draining; completed worker reports are delivered before queued user prompts.

nodes.label: ChangeFeed
nodes.rationale: Owns listeners, version counters and the 50 ms streaming throttle.

nodes.label: SessionAgent and RuntimeHost
nodes.rationale: An agent owns its transcript, model, credential and runtime; RuntimeHost supplies session-owned prompt, permissions, MCP identity and escalation handling.

nodes.label: ACP Runtime
nodes.rationale: One ACP session plus its process and forked sessions; warm and natively resumed runtimes receive only the new turn, while fresh ones receive a transcript recap.

nodes.label: Vendor launch specifications
nodes.rationale: launch.ts contains the per-vendor command, credential environment and shared Launch.session configuration for new, forked and resumed sessions.

nodes.label: Credential providers
nodes.rationale: Providers own credential priority, profile isolation, sign-in and allowance, but no wire protocol or turn loop. An API-key Codex credential has a separate home to avoid inherited ChatGPT authentication.

nodes.label: Model and vendor catalog
nodes.rationale: MODELS and VENDOR_INFO centralize facts; a new model is one row, while vendor integration also requires launch, registry, login, usage and persistence enum updates.

nodes.label: Default session and worker routing
nodes.rationale: Architecture text describes router.ts choosing an initial session model and a worker's model and depth when unspecified. Historical Jev design documents elsewhere in this chunk explicitly say Jev routing was removed.

nodes.label: Sirus loopback MCP server
nodes.rationale: One ephemeral loopback HTTP server serves all runtimes; per-session bearer tokens and caller names bind requests to their owner. Tools are listed per request so memory toggles apply immediately.

nodes.label: Sirus delegation tools
nodes.rationale: SpawnAgent, CheckAgent, MessageAgent, CancelAgent and ListAgents expose Sirus workers. Audience filtering hides delegation tools from workers.

nodes.label: Session-owned background workers
nodes.rationale: Completion queues an owner-directed report and wakes the owner when no turn, rewind, compaction or restore holds the session. Foreground waits become background work on owner cancellation or the tool wait limit.

nodes.label: WorkerRecord persistence
nodes.rationale: Snapshots preserve runs; a working run reopens as interrupted with no live agent, its report enters the owner's next prompt, and nothing restarts automatically. Later messaging can reopen the worker's native session.

nodes.label: Worker worktree isolation
nodes.rationale: Git workers run from project HEAD on sirus/<id> branches under the data directory. Removing the session removes worktrees but preserves branches; non-repositories run workers in place.

nodes.label: FORKED_WORKER_HANDOVER
nodes.rationale: Both vendors retain the owner's system prompt on fork, so the worker contract is supplied in its first prompt; failed forks fall back to text seeding from the owner record.

nodes.label: Vendor permission modes
nodes.rationale: ask, auto and bypass map to standard, auto_review and full_access. Sirus queues vendor escalations and returns vendor-provided options; it keeps no allowance or judge of its own.

nodes.label: ACP form elicitation
nodes.rationale: Vendor user questions become per-session forms queued behind approvals; adapter-marked free text becomes Other. Worker questions are declined immediately, and approval/question waits do not count as watchdog silence.

nodes.label: Vendor-native skills and skillPrompt
nodes.rationale: Claude receives user/project skill plugins plus enabled installed plugins; Codex discovers its own skill folders. Sirus rewrites /name into vendor syntax, keeps recap context in a separate block and sends images before command text.

nodes.label: Native session recovery
nodes.rationale: Saved vendor ID, original directory, credential source, profile home and prompt hash permit resume after restart or process loss. Same-home credentials can reuse history; missing or incompatible state falls back to a bounded recap with a notice.

nodes.label: Runtime-owned compaction
nodes.rationale: Each runtime compacts itself and reports a boundary; Session.compact sends /compact to the default participant. Sirus has no automatic compaction loop.

nodes.label: quietFor watchdog
nodes.rationale: Measures runtime silence excluding user-approval waits and running tools; status appears after one minute and unattended workers stop after 15 minutes.

nodes.label: Snapshot-only persistence and typed settings
nodes.rationale: Persistence reads/writes plain snapshots and normalizes older files without depending on runtime code. openSettings preserves unknown keys; Session.fromSnapshot rebuilds the domain object.

nodes.label: CommandSpec and CommandSession
nodes.rationale: Commands receive a structural Session subset and opt-in image/quit capabilities; registry order determines menus.

nodes.label: WorkerStrip and SpawnAgent transcript row
nodes.rationale: The strip reads the mutable run index directly, shows the freshest active/recent run and freezes ordering during keyboard focus. The original SpawnAgent row displays the completed report as expanded Markdown.

nodes.label: C1 input editor and mentions: landed
nodes.rationale: Audit reports local commit 7431a60: long pastes collapse while full text remains in drafts, input is capped at eight visible rows, movement uses grapheme display widths, file results precede participant creation, and ordinary unknown @words remain prose.

nodes.label: Directory-scoped prompt history
nodes.rationale: Implemented in the audit: canonical-directory history retains the latest 1,000 entries; Sirus-only slash commands are excluded to keep credentials out, and image attachments remain separate.

nodes.label: External draft editor
nodes.rationale: Implemented private temporary drafts with VISUAL/EDITOR arguments, terminal suspension, readback and cleanup; defaults to vi.

nodes.label: C3 doctor and update notice: landed
nodes.rationale: Audit reports local commit 2796037: CLI and /doctor inspect actual bundled adapters, login/configuration, data access and git with bounded subprocesses; remote API-key validity is not tested. A versioned notice remains visible with sidebar collapsed.

nodes.label: Wave C pending dependencies
nodes.rationale: C1 slash-menu findings await B2; C2 findings await B1 and its worktree is unstarted; vim mode and status customization await C1/B2. No implementation or verification is claimed for these.

nodes.label: Named cross-provider review
nodes.rationale: Create a reviewer using @reviewer MODEL_ID and give it the relevant task and files, since it receives no earlier turns. Both providers must be connected for cross-provider review, and only one participant should edit overlapping files at a time.

nodes.label: Inspectable useful result
nodes.rationale: Evaluate a checked change or actionable explanation yourself; agreement between two models is not proof of correctness.

nodes.label: File-only checkpoint undo
nodes.rationale: /undo files restores checkpointed files and preserves chat; it may overwrite later personal edits and cannot undo external effects.

nodes.label: Persisted native-session reference
nodes.rationale: Implemented reference records vendor, ID, original directory, credential source, profile home and system-prompt hash for participants and workers.

nodes.label: Resume-first recovery and replay suppression
nodes.rationale: Prefer advertised session/resume, use session/load only when resume is unavailable, preserve requested IDs if responses omit them, and drain pending SDK notifications before admitting new transcript output. Configuration and background-task updates remain live.

nodes.label: Credential-home affinity
nodes.rationale: Try the saved credential first; another credential may reuse the session only in the same profile home. Missing or changed state produces a notice and recap fallback; vendor logs are never copied across homes.

nodes.label: Native-history invalidation
nodes.rationale: Rewind, clear, incompatible or unapplied model changes, and system-prompt changes start fresh. Sirus chat forks must not reuse the original native ID, while owner-context worker forks use genuine ACP forks.

nodes.label: Native recovery verification
nodes.rationale: Document reports typecheck and 590 tests passing normally and with color, plus live Claude/Codex participant and worker restart recall and actual missing-session refusals. Live account revocation and a 30-second unresponsive cancellation were not induced.

nodes.label: Planned facade decomposition
nodes.rationale: Plan proposes splitting Session, providers, tools/permissions, persistence and memory behind small interfaces while preserving public behavior and making extension local; its checkboxes are a plan, not proof of completion.

nodes.label: Refactor dependency ordering
nodes.rationale: Plan orders dead-code cleanup; session alongside memory; tools before providers because transports must first consume turn.toolbox; persistence alongside commands/frontend; then final review.

nodes.label: Planned characterization and compatibility checks
nodes.rationale: Calls for existing test preservation, explicit empty-failed-bubble and shell-classifier coverage, a secret-containing-spaces test, scratch data isolation, typecheck, full suites and final TUI smoke verification.

nodes.label: UI identity and version contract
nodes.rationale: Historical audit identifies stable getMessages identity, version counters, session-ID remounts and in-place message mutation before throttled notifications as load-bearing frontend contracts.

nodes.label: Message-count send acceptance
nodes.rationale: Historical Chat infers acceptance from message-array length, coupling sendMessage behavior to attachment retention, draft restoration and draft promotion.

nodes.label: Exit-save persistence
nodes.rationale: Exit handlers must save the already-mutated record even before a throttled notification arrives; the audit identifies an existing round-trip test.

nodes.label: Persistence, memory, commands and miscellaneous audit (2026-09-07)
Historical persistence-domain cycle
nodes.rationale: Audit finds persistence importing Session while runtime components depend back on storage, duplicated legacy reconstruction, and unknown settings stripped by parsing; proposes plain snapshots and read-through preservation.

nodes.label: Memory schema migration and vector reindex
nodes.rationale: Historical v1-v3 migration depends on checking vector-table existence before creation; embedder changes trigger reindex, global/project scope boundaries constrain links, and available search merges global with this project.

nodes.label: Command secret string-reentry defect
nodes.rationale: Audit reports collected API keys appended to a command string and split on spaces, losing secret boundaries; registry-bypassing permission shortcuts are another frontend coupling.

nodes.label: Duplicated protected-text scanners
nodes.rationale: Audit finds fileSearch protectedText and mentions scanning similar but not proven equivalent at unterminated delimiters; differential testing is required before unification.

nodes.label: Historical test-isolation hazards
nodes.rationale: Audit identifies mixed directory injection/environment overrides, module-level caches and no shared setup; missing overrides can write to the real store.

nodes.label: Historical Provider / ModelStrategy coupling
nodes.rationale: One vendor object combined model dispatch, credentials, auth UI and fallback; model identity was lost and model facts duplicated across four edit sites.

nodes.label: Historical credential fallback invariants
nodes.rationale: Preserve per-runtime stickiness, no fallback after abort, no replay of delegated tools with unknown outcomes, completed tool-work carryover and masked exhaustion errors.

nodes.label: Historical global active-source defect
nodes.rationale: A single currentSource slot could display whichever agent most recently started a turn despite concurrent runtimes; the audit calls for per-runtime tracking while keeping live sidebar updates.

nodes.label: Historical cross-vendor runtime leak
nodes.rationale: resetRuntime resolved via the current model's vendor while model changes did not reset, orphaning a Claude child after switching to GPT until a global reset.

nodes.label: Historical Session god class
nodes.rationale: The audit records 952 lines, 17 responsibilities, a 14-positional-argument constructor, duplicated mention grammar, global directory locks and index-correlated round arrays.

nodes.label: Historical round and bubble semantics
nodes.rationale: Preserve parallel user mentions, coalesced peer invocations, self-mention exclusion, immediate cancellation, retained partial output and removal of never-streamed failed bubbles. The erase path lacked direct coverage.

nodes.label: Historical mutating-tool checkpoint barrier
nodes.rationale: At audit time providers could start immediately while mutating tools awaited beforeMutation; the barrier also had to settle on cancellation. This predates the native-tool architecture's checkpoint-before-prompt design.

nodes.label: Historical queued-command policy
nodes.rationale: FIFO prompt draining must work without a mounted Chat, but a queued slash command pauses itself and everything behind it; queues were not persisted.

nodes.label: Historical subagent audience-enforcement gap
nodes.rationale: Audience filtering applied only during listing, so direct SpawnAgent execution could create a grandchild; the proposed toolbox must reject non-visible tools at execution.

nodes.label: Historical shell classifier
nodes.rationale: A roughly 250-line parser had no direct tests and RunShell could be classified three times; unknown tools defaulted to read only safely because the runtime rejected them first.

nodes.label: Historical tool/provider import cycle
nodes.rationale: tools/agents read modelStrategies through chat while chat imported the tool runtime; lazy schema access concealed the cycle.

nodes.label: Filesystem barrier inside permission context
nodes.rationale: Audit separates beforeMutation from authorization: RunShell always waits even for read-classified commands and bypass mode, because checkpoint safety is independent of approval policy.

nodes.label: Subsystem facades and injected collaborators
nodes.rationale: Approved target, not a completion record: preserve behavior while making responsibilities narrow, extension local and process-wide defaults injectable.

nodes.label: Proposed Transcript RoundHandle
nodes.rationale: publish, update, settle and discardIfEmpty would own assistant-bubble identity in place of parallel arrays and indexOf splices; the later architecture assigns round-entry identity to Timeline.

nodes.label: Proposed per-turn Toolbox
nodes.rationale: Transports would receive visible tools plus run(call), separating barrier, authorization, execution and formatting; runtime audience checks close the grandchild hole and remove transport imports of the tool registry.

nodes.label: Proposed provider catalog, sources, transport and fallback layers
nodes.rationale: Pure model facts, one credential source store, host/delegated transport contracts and verbatim fallback policy replace ModelStrategy; this design precedes the ACP-only migration.

nodes.label: Proposed plain-snapshot repository
nodes.rationale: File-format normalization belongs in persistence; Session accepts only modern snapshots. Typed read-through settings preserve unknown fields and avoid cache-sensitive test failures.

nodes.label: Proposed structural CommandContext
nodes.rationale: Commands depend on a narrow CommandSession with optional image/quit capabilities; secrets are passed as argument values and permission shortcuts use the registry.

nodes.label: Proposed MemoryStore port and factory
nodes.rationale: Five methods save/get/delete/search/close over MemoryTarget, with schema and vector index separated and directory-keyed stores replacing the first-use singleton.

nodes.label: Multi-vendor cockpit migration: draft for approval
Proposed ACP-only vendor runtime migration
nodes.rationale: Draft replaces direct API transports and Sirus's agent loop with Claude/Codex native harnesses over ACP; launch specs isolate vendor differences and exact adapter pins limit protocol drift.

nodes.label: Proposed addressed participant transcripts
nodes.rationale: Only directed messages enter each participant's record; whole attributed sender messages avoid losing assumed context, and the merged timeline is a derived UI/snapshot view.

nodes.label: Proposed loopback HTTP MCP bridge
nodes.rationale: One server exposes Sirus memory/delegation with session token and participant identity; MCP-over-ACP was unstable and unsupported by both verified adapters.

nodes.label: Proposed vendor-owned permission review
nodes.rationale: Mode kinds replace Sirus's classifier/judge and render vendor escalation options. The draft notes differing Claude/Codex sandbox and auto-mode behavior, requiring surfaced fallback status.

nodes.label: Proposed pre-prompt checkpoint
nodes.rationale: Native tools cannot wait on host barriers, so capture must finish before prompting; session-wide sequence numbers support rewind across independent transcripts.

nodes.label: Proposed vendor-native compaction
nodes.rationale: Advertising session.compaction exposes vendor compaction boundaries, and /compact passes through as a prompt; shared-transcript compaction is removed.

nodes.label: Draft defers elicitation support
nodes.rationale: This draft does not advertise elicitation.form or allow AskUserQuestion, although it identifies ACP form support; current architecture in this chunk documents that support as present.

nodes.label: Jev session routing: historical approved design
Removed Jev session-model routing
nodes.rationale: Historical design selected a new session's model through TypeSafe AI System One. The document explicitly states Jev routing has since been removed and sessions use the saved preference or default.

nodes.label: Historical latest-model routing candidates
nodes.rationale: One latest model per credentialed vendor with allowance; API keys and unknown cached usage count as available, one candidate bypasses Jev, and no candidates preserve fallback.

nodes.label: Historical bounded confidence fallback
nodes.rationale: Explicit user choice wins; missing JEV_API, a two-second timeout without retry, errors or confidence below 0.5 retain the starting model silently.

nodes.label: Historical ModelProfile routing criteria
nodes.rationale: Profiles combine researched strengths, named/date-specific benchmarks, practical reviews and token prices; live allowance is rendered alongside each candidate instead of stored in catalog facts.

nodes.label: Proposed worker completion wakes owner
nodes.rationale: The historical worker design delivers terminal reports into the owner's transcript and starts its next turn; reports wait while busy and precede user-queued prompts. Escape cancels only the foreground turn.

nodes.label: Proposed worker worktree isolation
nodes.rationale: Workers branch from project HEAD without uncommitted changes or ignored directories, preserving branches after session cleanup and allowing project-file rewind while isolated workers run.

nodes.label: Proposed owner-context fork and steering
nodes.rationale: ACP fork shares the owner's process but uses worker callbacks and MCP identity; the first prompt carries the worker contract. Mid-run messages use _session/steering; this historical version refuses messages to finished workers.

nodes.label: Proposed persisted WorkerRecord
nodes.rationale: Snapshots hold transcript, branch, status and report; restored working runs become interrupted records, do not restart and report on the owner's next prompt.

nodes.label: Removed Jev worker-model routing
nodes.rationale: Historical proposal chose model and thinking level from allowance-qualified candidates except Haiku, with owner model/level fallback. The document explicitly says Jev routing was removed and current selection rules now apply.

nodes.label: Proposed multi-line worker strip
nodes.rationale: Historical spec proposes one line per worker with running first and finished lines dimmed until dismissal; current architecture instead describes one freshest-run line with a counter.

nodes.label: Command file-layout rule
nodes.rationale: One commands.ts per domain folder; behavior.ts is justified by outside consumers. session/ remains an explicit temporary exception despite no external behavior consumer.

nodes.label: CommandSession structural interface
nodes.rationale: Commands see only the conversation methods they use; attaching images and quitting require opt-in capabilities the caller may not supply.

nodes.label: Ordered command registry
nodes.rationale: Every spec is registered once, and registry order is reflected in slash-menu and help display.

nodes.label: Active-installation dashboard
nodes.rationale: Responsive day/week/month cards present rolling estimates, explicitly warning that fabricated public submissions may be included; an aria-live status reports loading, update or failure.

nodes.label: Configurable statistics API base
nodes.rationale: API URL precedence is query parameter api, window.SIRUS_STATS_API_URL, then the sirus-stats Worker default; a trailing slash is removed.

nodes.label: loadStats
nodes.rationale: Fetches /stats as JSON, rejects non-OK responses and non-safe-integer or negative counts, updates day/week/month displays and status, and catches failures into an unavailable message.

nodes.label: setCount
nodes.rationale: Formats numeric counts using Number(value).toLocaleString and writes textContent.

nodes.label: setStatus
nodes.rationale: Writes accessible status text and toggles the error CSS class.

nodes.label: Session-scoped model, cancellation and subagent state
nodes.rationale: Checklist marks model changes, Escape cancellation and active-subagent counts as scoped to the current session; checkmarks are reported claims, not independent verification.

nodes.label: Save partial responses when quitting
nodes.rationale: Checklist marks retaining response progress on quit and the command-header state fix as complete.

nodes.label: Cancelled turns finalize running tools
nodes.rationale: Checklist marks failing all open tools and stopping running-command display after cancellation as complete.

nodes.label: Skills and heartbeat support
nodes.rationale: Checklist marks skills and a heartbeat mechanism complete without implementation details.

nodes.label: Show transcript — what it has said and done so far (selected)
Send a message — steer it while it works
Cancel — stop it and keep what it has done

hyperedges.label: Addressed multi-participant round and timeline flow
Native recovery safety and fallback contract
